risks.title: Regulatory Risk on Ride-hailing and Gig Workers
risks.score_rationale: Grab's 20-F flags evolving regulation on driver classification, minimum earnings, vehicle quotas and ride pricing across Singapore, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam and the Philippines. New rules could materially increase driver costs.
risks.summary: Tightening regulation on driver classification, minimum pay and fleet quotas across Southeast Asia could increase operating costs and constrain supply.

risks.title: Competition (GoTo, Sea, ByteDance, Banks)
risks.score_rationale: Grab competes with GoTo, ShopeeFood, foodpanda, TikTok Shop, regional banks and emerging super-apps. Rational pricing in Indonesia is uncertain; incentive wars erode margins.
risks.summary: Aggressive competition from GoTo, Sea, foodpanda and emerging entrants could force higher incentive spend and delay segment profitability.

risks.title: Digital Banking Investment and Credit Losses
risks.score_rationale: GXS Bank (Singapore), GXBank (Malaysia) and Superbank (Indonesia) require continued capital injections and incur start-up losses. Credit losses on unsecured lending could escalate.
risks.summary: Continued losses and capital needs from digital bank ventures, plus rising unsecured credit losses, could pressure consolidated profitability.

risks.title: Path to Sustained Profitability
risks.score_rationale: Despite recent adjusted EBITDA breakeven, Grab's GAAP profitability and free cash flow remain limited. Investor focus on profitability transition adds execution pressure.
risks.summary: Failure to scale to sustained GAAP profitability while balancing growth investment could pressure valuation and access to capital.

risks.title: FX, Macro and Southeast Asia Country Risk
risks.score_rationale: Operations span eight countries with diverse FX, inflation and political risk profiles. Indonesian rupiah and Thai baht volatility, plus political transitions, impact reported results.
risks.summary: Currency volatility and political/economic uncertainty across Southeast Asian markets could disrupt operations and translate negatively to reported results.

risks.title: Cybersecurity and Data Privacy
risks.score_rationale: Grab processes large volumes of user, driver and merchant personal and financial data across multiple privacy regimes (PDPA Singapore, Indonesia PDP Law, Malaysia PDPA). Breach risk is heightened by digital banking.
risks.summary: Cybersecurity breaches and divergent data privacy regulations across ASEAN markets could result in fines, user attrition and remediation costs.

risks.title: Driver and Merchant Supply Constraints
risks.score_rationale: Service levels depend on driver-partner and merchant participation. Driver shortages, attrition to competitors and merchant churn affect order completion and service quality.
risks.summary: Difficulty attracting and retaining drivers and merchants could degrade service levels, raise incentives spend and limit revenue growth.
